metadata.original_issue: GitHub Issue #183887: RuntimeError during torch.compile Inductor fake tensor execution on int64 addmm/in-place addmm comparison

knowledge_abstraction.bug_theme: Fake tensor propagation and dtype constraint violation under graph compilation
knowledge_abstraction.general_principle: Compiler backends and fake tensor propagation may make dtype-specific assumptions, causing runtime failures or eager/compiled divergence when uncommon integer dtypes or operation variants are used.

risk_dimensions.shape: Unusual, non-contiguous, or expanded tensor shapes under compilation may interact with lowering and fake tensor propagation.
risk_dimensions.dtype: Integer dtype boundary cases, especially int64 and int32, can expose incorrect fake tensor or backend handling.
risk_dimensions.memory: Non-contiguous or expanded memory layouts may violate hidden assumptions during compiled lowering.
risk_dimensions.device: Compiler backend lowering may behave differently across CPU and accelerator devices.
risk_dimensions.execution_state: Compilation state with torch.compile and fake tensor execution path; eager versus compiled execution divergence, especially for in-place and out-of-place operation variants.

failure_mechanism.description: Compiler backend lowering and fake tensor propagation may not correctly handle integer dtype constraints for in-place and out-of-place operations, leading to runtime exceptions or eager/compiled divergence.

input_exploration: Vary integer dtypes such as int32 and int64 across tensor operations
Include non-contiguous or expanded tensor variants where supported
Compare in-place and out-of-place operation analogs under identical logical data
constraint_awareness: Compilation with Inductor and fake tensor propagation can enforce stricter dtype or layout constraints than eager execution
In-place and out-of-place operations may diverge under graph lowering
Fake tensor validation can reject valid integer dtype cases during compiled execution
oracle_strategy: Use eager execution as the reference for numerical equivalence
Monitor for runtime exceptions during compilation or fake tensor propagation

transferability.reason: The underlying principle applies to compiled operators that rely on fake tensor propagation and backend lowering with integer dtype handling. It is not limited to one API, although the risk is most pronounced for operations with in-place/out-of-place variants and dtype-specific lowering paths.

important_considerations: Explore compiled versus eager consistency for integer dtype operations
Include both in-place and out-of-place operation variants
Exercise fake tensor propagation paths with compiler backends such as Inductor
Introduce non-contiguous or expanded tensor layouts
generation_strategy: Generate API-agnostic harnesses that compare eager and compiler-backed execution under varied integer dtypes, memory layouts, and in-place/out-of-place variants, using reference outputs and exception monitoring to expose graph transformation and dtype boundary issues.
